De naso elephanti fortis longo & flexibili ad modum serpentis sed in elephante sit eminentior cunctis bestijs inclinatio ad pascendum non per decem sine motu est quia possit tanti corporis moles.

**Prasius** lapis est viridissimus ut natura est herbe. hic lapis viriditatem habet admirabilem sed est frequens. sed herbe viri- nomine propriam viriditatem hic lapis non caret vicio namque quum sit virens nichilominus atramento uelut maculis aspersis obscuratur. Quattuor autem species eius sunt. Tres enim morem invisum habent. Vna est gipsata. alia fulva. et tercia maculis aspersa. Sunt qui dicunt hunc lapidem carere vicio. set rationabilius est et verum. set aliquas habet maculas sordidas quas se in substantia permixtas habet. Vnde et aliter dicitur in summa namque dicitur prasium lapidem esse preciosum et vult queri aurum. Querit ergo proprietatem mortuorum ad lapidem et de hiis que dicuntur per fidem <unclear>metiri</unclear> consuevi vult. Dicunt ergo de lapide que vulgo prasini vocantur. Aliqui de quibusdam qui habent aliquam substantiam mortem id est tristiciam corporis possident. Qui quia quidam lapis propter maris venti et aquis abundantiam ad p<unclear>er</unclear>va se fecerit detractam uocata triualla (?) th<unclear>u</unclear>m huius rei probatio videtur quod prasius ille color alicuius nubes (?) candore amiserit sua.

**Sapphirus** lapis preciosissimus qui de regio dicitur lapis hic tenet colorem aeris de magis preciosis qui ex partibus orientis mittitur. Hic conservat corpus et membra integra vegetatque vigore in interiore et frigidat sudore fervidis collo exortus refriget dolore valet frigidus p<unclear>er</unclear>hibetur et citat gratias ex merito illius hominis qui religionem suam native tenuerit de colore per fugationem dicitur non debere d<unclear>omini</unclear> ad vicia profanari. set contra invidia ignis huic ad parte non grosus est et fortis ut ille qui portat eum primo subdio captivate fuerit suppositio lapidis sapphyri fuit qui per pri-

uilegium fuit maxima per d<unclear>eum</unclear> quia siliud quilibet m<unclear>eruerit</unclear> tempore precatore sapphyri dicitur optimimi fuit et vno fit preciui exercitui fuit et virtutis non sapphyri optimi fuit in magis alij qui videntur p<unclear>er</unclear>splendet eo quod eos videtur ipse uidetur quod obfuscatione coloris densior (?) sunt et quida sapphyri orientales qui mittunt lapidem amiserit bunt (?) atque merito eorum fuerit virtutum potentiis dei.

**Smaragdus** lapis preciosissimus est et vnus de xij lapidibus preciosis omnibus rebus virtutis precellit et virens est ultra opes et quia <unclear>sivia</unclear> dicitur hunc lapidem dismansse (?) eius gripis (?) multus aurei pruna edentatas fuerunt illi populi id est gens <unclear>vasta</unclear> potrat secures preliat vnde acre viciunt dicitur quovis obfuscitum per se ut herba rubet vmbrosam flori set optia est plena quoniam prata de admiranti videntur videtur fugat adinvicem decentibus de visum tenuatus erigat oculos aquas attingunt vno visum penitus reddit viren<unclear>s</unclear> et in dubio suis opes ampliat et eos qui altera sint tantis malis tempestates ampascit et lassatos motu.

**Sardonix** lapis est de duobus lapidibus fit natus proprius scilicet (?) sardio (?) et <unclear>alido</unclear> propterea dicitur ex xij (?) lapidibus supra ad albet et impete propterea est et hujus coloras (?) preciosi fuerunt vale dicitur quoniam per lune menstruum videtur ex innumeris rerum (?) Sed destitutas moliit(?) hunc stabilem in aspectu ubi perdonis (?) presius (?) est nec non per omnibus (?) set pulcherrimus erit ubi opacitati prima hic lapis rera nefit qualle (?) precedate vices ea et huic qui perptat hunc (?)

--- Page 443 ---
<language>Latin</language>
<page-type>illustration</page-type>
<page-num>108</page-num>

<image-desc>
This page features two horizontal registers of hand-colored alchemical or allegorical illustrations.

In the upper register, a red, four-wheeled chariot is being pulled to the left by a team of four reddish-brown horses. A black, horned demonic figure with a long tail and a protruding tongue stands atop the horses, holding the reins. Seated in the chariot is a figure wearing a golden crown and a red robe with a white-and-grey checkered lining; this figure holds a personified radiant sun in their left hand.

The lower register contains two distinct scenes. On the left, a man in a red tunic and white leggings lies back against a dark, rocky outcrop. He is being attended to by a woman with blonde hair wearing a long green dress and a white veil. To the right, another woman in identical green attire reaches out to take the hands of a man who is submerged up to his chest in a golden-yellow pool. From a dark cloud suspended in the air above them, several long, wavy tongues of yellow and red flame descend toward the figure in the pool.
</image-desc>

<vocab>chariot, sun, demon, horses, pool, flames, alchemy</vocab>

--- Page 444 ---
<language>Latin</language>
<page-type>illustration</page-type>

<image-desc>
A full-page medieval manuscript illustration depicting the god Apollo as leader of the Muses (Apollo Musagetes). Apollo is portrayed as a crowned king in silver plate armor, seated upon a throne that grows like a tree from the center of a golden, four-wheeled chariot. He holds a large bow and an arrow. A black raven is perched on the front edge of the chariot. The chariot is drawn by four horses (two white, two dappled brown) led by a driver wearing a red hooded cloak and hat. 

To the left of the chariot stand the nine Muses, depicted as women in contemporary medieval dress. Each Muse is identified by a red banner containing her name in Gothic script:
1. Pronuntiato (associated with Calliope)
2. Prima (associated with Urania)
3. Terpsicore
4. Erato
5. Palimnia (Polyhymnia)
6. Talia (Thalia)
7. Euterpe
8. Melpomene
9. Clio
</image-desc>

<page-type>illustration</page-type>

<image-desc>
This manuscript page contains a large-scale illustration rich in alchemical or allegorical symbolism, set against a plain parchment background.

In the center, a nude, bearded man (likely representing the Alchemical King) stands in profile facing right. He has long, wavy brown hair and two grey horns protruding from his head. He wears an ornate golden crown, above which floats a thin circular golden halo. His right hand is clasped with the hand of a woman standing to his right. He also holds a tall, slender golden staff that terminates in a two-pronged, trident-like tip.

The woman (likely Sapientia or the Alchemical Queen) is dressed in a long, heavy red gown featuring grey vertical panels and a wide black belt. She wears a white wimple that covers her head and neck. She looks upward, pointing her right index finger toward the sky.

In the upper right corner, a red-winged seraph or cherub head appears within a blue, semi-circular cloud. A series of golden droplets or rays descend from this cloud toward the woman.

On the left side of the composition, three hybrid creatures are depicted with the bodies, wings, and feathered legs of brown birds and the heads of women. Three golden bowls are placed before them; the middle creature is shown leaning forward to drink from one of these bowls.

There is no original text on this folio; the fragmentary Latin text visible on the far right edge belongs to the facing page across the manuscript gutter.
</image-desc>

<vocab>Alchemical King, Sapientia, seraph, harpy, siren, trident, crown, wimple, allegory</vocab>

A full-page alchemical or allegorical illumination. 

The central figure is a bearded king seated on a golden throne beneath a canopy with a green and black checkered roof. The king is blindfolded with a white cloth tied around his head. Resting on his crown is a grey ram's head. He is dressed in a vibrant yellow robe decorated with numerous red-outlined eagles and wears a black belt with three golden rosettes. In his right hand, he holds a green lily branch; in his left, a golden globus cruciger (orb and cross). A long, curved grey blade or tail extends from beneath the front of his robes.

At the top of the illumination, a blue cloud with a yellow center emits golden rays and red flames toward the throne. Six large black birds, resembling ravens or crows, are arranged around the king: two at the top, two flanking the midsection, and two at the bottom.

In the lower register of the page, a woman in a long green gown kneels in profile facing left. To her right stands a grey goat with prominent horns. In the bottom right corner, a seventh black creature—a bird with a long, serpentine tail—faces the center. The background of the entire scene is the natural color of the parchment.
</image-desc>

<image-desc>
A hand-colored illustration depicting the Roman/Greek myth of Saturn (Cronus) and Ops (Rhea). 

Centrally seated upon an elaborate golden throne under a blue and red canopy are two figures. To the left is Saturn, represented as an elderly man with a long grey beard, wearing a red hat and a red robe trimmed with ermine fur. He holds a large scythe in his right hand and appears to be in the process of consuming one of his children. To his right sits Ops, wearing a golden crown and a flowing green gown, holding a golden bowl containing a small infant.

In the foreground, a figure wearing a crown and a green feathered tunic (likely Jupiter) offers a swaddled object, representing the stone given to Saturn in place of the child, to the seated pair. Below this exchange, three other children are depicted: one in a pinkish-white tunic walking toward the center, another in a yellow-and-red striped garment reaching out, and two more infants sitting together on a green mound in the lower right corner. 

The scene is framed by two tall golden spires topped with fleur-de-lis ornaments. The background throne architecture features Gothic-style arched niches.
</image-desc>

This manuscript page consists of two horizontal miniature illustrations, likely depicting planetary influences or allegorical triumphs.

The top illustration depicts a king wearing a golden crown and a purple robe, seated within the battlements of a pink, octagonal fortress or tower. From a dark cloud directly above him, golden rays or droplets fall upon his head. The fortress is surrounded by a large company of armed soldiers. On the left, the soldiers wear diverse headgear, including hoods and blue kettle hats; one prominent figure in the foreground wears golden scale armor and a wide-brimmed brown hat, holding a decorative shield. On the right, another group of soldiers is gathered, featuring one man in full yellow plate armor. The soldiers carry a variety of polearms, including halberds, pikes, and spears.

The bottom illustration shows a scene mounted on a large, four-wheeled yellow wagon. Under a yellow wooden canopy, a king in a blue gown and a queen in a pink gown are seated together, appearing to hold hands. To their right, the wagon carries a large black hellmouth shaped like a beast's head with a wide, toothy maw. Inside the flaming mouth, several figures are being consumed, including a crowned king and a tonsured monk. The wagon is pulled to the left by a team of three animals: a dark, bristly beast (possibly a boar) and two yellow lions. A crowned youth in a red tunic and a long, billowing red cloak sits astride the lead lion, guiding the team with a small rod.
</image-desc>

The bottom miniature shows a symbolic or pastoral scene set against a background of dense green foliage. # Hic consequenter depingitur Imago Fortune

<image-desc>A detailed manuscript illustration depicting the "Image of Fortune." A crowned woman sits within a four-wheeled yellow chariot. She wears a wimple and a dark green robe adorned with a floral pattern. In her left hand, she holds a long golden scepter topped with a complex floral ornament. A peacock, featuring a small halo above its head, perches upon her right hand. The chariot is pulled by two lions, each of which is being ridden by a monkey acting as a driver. The drawing is rendered in ink and wash colors on parchment. Several faint circular watermarks from the Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana are visible across the center of the page.</image-desc>

<image-desc>
The bottom half of the page features two large, hand-colored allegorical illustrations corresponding to the text above. 

On the left, a crowned man in a red and white tunic, labeled in red as 'Imago libidinis et luxurie', rides a large green chimaera or dragon. The creature has multiple heads: its main dragon head is devouring a person, while other heads, including a human one looking backwards, emerge from its neck and back. The beast's sharp claws trample several human figures on the ground. The man holds a long spear or staff.

On the right, a woman in a long white gown with a dark belt, labeled 'Imago adulationis', stands holding a round mirror that reflects a face. To her right is a tall, ornate golden structure resembling a fountain or a multi-tiered lamp. Green leafy plants grow at her feet.
</image-desc>
